svg.title: Bowline formed, backed with a stopper and checked
svg.desc: Loose bowline in utility cord. The standing part runs up to the load. A small overhand loop is formed in the standing part with the working side on top. The working end comes up through that loop, passes behind the standing part and goes back down through the loop beside its first pass, so the tail finishes inside the fixed loop, where an overhand stopper is tied with tail to spare. A smaller view shows the failure to avoid: a short tail with no stopper, which can work loose. Utility loads only; not for climbing or life-safety use. Conceptual drawing, not to scale.
svg.text: Z09-P14 · TECHNICAL REVIEW · NOT TO SCALE
Utility loads only. Never use a camp-cord bowline for climbing, rescue or life support.
